transcript:
HEADER: 2027-03-30T16:00:00-07:00 | Duration 48 mins
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE); Liam Chen (Redwood SE); Daniel Ortiz (Elysium, Head of Search); Priya Nair (Elysium, ML Eng); Marcus Lee (Elysium, CTO)

Summary: Quick discovery to understand Elysium's current vector search stack, performance pain points, and evaluate Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for an embeddings + reranking POC. Discussed vector DB options, throughput targets, embedding dimensionality, hybrid BM25 + dense rerank approach, and security/compliance requirements. Agreed to run a benchmark POC on Dedicated with 1k QPS target and share security docs.

Topics: current search architecture; vector DB integration; embedding dimension & model choice; throughput/latency; hybrid search & reranking; deployment models; security & data residency; POC next steps

00:00 Samira: Hey everyone, Samira from Redwood here, thanks for joining, quick intro — I'm AE, and Liam our solutions engineer will go deep technical — you all good with the agenda? 
00:08 Daniel: Yeah thanks, Daniel here, we'll try to keep it under an hour, Priya and Marcus on — Priya runs the embedding infra, Marcus cares about cost and compliance. 
00:18 Liam: Cool, quick high-level — Redwood supports hosted API for quick dev, Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, and Private (VPC/on prem) for compliance. Today we'll focus on embeddings and reranking options. 
00:29 Priya: Our stack today is ElasticSearch for BM25 + Pinecone for dense vectors, we do hybrid search where we BM25 the top 200 then rerank with a dense model. Cost is spiking when we scale and latency spikes under load. 
00:45 Liam: Got it. What's your current corpus size and typical query QPS? 
00:51 Daniel: Corpus is around 120M documents, embeddings stored in Pinecone, we do 200 QPS steady and spike to 1k with seasonal loads. Latency target is 200ms 95p end-to-end for search + rerank but currently closer to 400-500ms during spikes. 
01:12 Samira: Thanks, that's helpful. Are you encoding embeddings with a single dimension size today? Which model/dim? 
01:19 Priya: We're using 1536-d embeddings from a third-party model (OpenAI ada-ish), trying smaller dims causes recall drop, so we've been cautious. 
01:29 Liam: Two levers — you can reduce dim with a quantized model or use Knowledge Distillation to keep perf, or move to a Dedicated runtime with better batching and KV cache policies to reduce cost/latency. 
01:44 Marcus: For Dedicated we need to understand pricing and isolation — can you commit to not co-locating others on the same GPU pool? 
01:52 Samira: Yes, Dedicated is reserved capacity — you get your own GPU pool with isolation guarantees and SLA-backed latency/uptime; we'll share the pricing and sizing spreadsheet after. 
02:02 Daniel: If we go Private/VPC, how does data residency and KMS work? 
02:09 Liam: Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and you can keep data in your VPC or on-prem — the control plane still authenticates but the inference plane is in your network. We also provide audit logs and optional increased retention for observability. 
02:24 Priya: One problem currently is Pinecone's vector indexing overhead for 120M - reindex cost is high. Is Redwood recommending a specific vector DB? 
02:34 Liam: We are DB-agnostic — you can plug in Milvus, Weaviate, Pinecone or an S3-backed ANN store. For large corpora we often recommend a hybrid: approximate nearest neighbor store for the first-pass and then a light-weight in-memory reranker on Dedicated to avoid network hops. Also prefix/KV caching helps if you have repeated prefixes. 
02:56 Daniel: How does the rerank step integrate? We do BM25 top-K then dense rerank, we want to keep same flow. 
03:05 Liam: That's standard — Redwood's API supports returning dense vectors and scores, and we have examples for doing hybrid search where you pass BM25 results into a reranker model pinned to the same Dedicated pool to avoid cross-network latency. We also have a 'rerank-as-a-service' pattern if you prefer. 
03:28 Priya: Can you run a rerank model with batching to improve throughput? Our current reranker is small but can't get to 1k QPS. 
03:36 Liam: Yes, Dedicated supports continuous batching and kernel selection tuned for the model size; batching increases throughput significantly. We can also quantize the reranker and use an int8 path. 
03:49 Marcus: Any tradeoffs with quantization and recall? 
03:53 Liam: Slight recall dip sometimes, depends on model. We recommend running an eval suite on your prompts — we'll set that up in the POC. Redwood Optimize can surface regressions tied to prompt sets. 
04:05 Daniel: On the dimensionality question — we don't want to lose semantic quality. Is it better to keep 1536 or try 768? 
04:13 Liam: Many customers move to 768 for a good latency/cost sweet spot, but for niche domain corpora 1536 sometimes helps. We'll recommend experiments in the POC: try both dims and compare MRR/recall and latency. 
04:29 Priya: About vector DB throughput — if we keep Pinecone, will the network hop between Pinecone and Redwood add latency? 
04:36 Liam: Yes, there's network overhead. For high QPS we suggest co-locating vectors in the same region or moving to an integrated store or storing keys and retrieving top-K then running rerank on Dedicated to eliminate round trips. 
04:50 Daniel: Security — we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, role-based access and audit logs, plus data residency for EU. Can you satisfy that? 
04:58 Samira: Yes — Redwood is SOC 2 Type II, supports SAML/SSO, RBAC, and we have EU regions and Private deployments for strict residency. We'll send SOC2 report and Private deployment checklist. 
05:10 Marcus: Any regulatory or legal surprises for log retention? We need logs for audits but also to meet retention limits. 
05:18 Liam: You can configure audit log retention and we support redaction for PII. For Private you control log storage. We'll share specifics in the security pack. 
05:29 Daniel: For the POC, expected timeline? We want something within 3 weeks. 
05:34 Samira: Sounds reasonable. Typical POC: week 1 onboarding + data ingest (we help with connectors), week 2 run benchmarks and evals, week 3 review and sizing recommendation. 
05:46 Priya: We can surface sample queries and a subset of corpus. How do you want dataset access? 
05:52 Liam: Ideally a 1-2% sample or 1M docs and the real query trace if possible. We'll provide a benchmark runbook to standardize the tests. 
06:04 Daniel: How do you measure recall/quality — do you have out-of-the-box metrics? 
06:09 Liam: We'll run MRR, recall@k, latency p95/p99, and a manual eval set for semantic quality. Redwood Optimize links regressions to prompt sets. 
06:20 Samira: Quick note — we'll also include Dedicated sizing guidance: GPU types, memory, and expected QPS per instance for common model sizes. 
06:28 Daniel: What about costs vs Hosted — if we start Hosted for dev then move to Dedicated for production, how big is the delta? 
06:34 Samira: Hosted is pay-as-you-go good for dev; Dedicated reduces per-token cost at scale but requires reserved commitment. We'll send a cost comparison example tailored to your 1k QPS target. 
06:46 Priya: Do you support custom embeddings models or only Redwood curated ones? 
06:50 Liam: You can bring your own model or use our curated models. For Private you can run customer models behind your firewall. We also support model version pinning and rollouts. 
07:02 Marcus: Network peering and VPC setup — what's the lead time? 
07:07 Samira: VPC peering can be done in a few days but depends on your infra team. For Private on-prem, it's longer — planning and security review usually 2-4 weeks. 
07:18 Daniel: OK let's talk benchmarks: we want 1k QPS score with rerank, target p95 300ms. Can you meet that on Dedicated? 
07:27 Liam: Likely yes with the right model size, batching, and GPU type; we'll test in the POC. We'll also try hybrid search to reduce rerank load by keeping top-K small. 
07:40 Priya: Do you have any references who've done a similar 120M doc scale POC? 
07:45 Samira: Yes, we ran a POC with a publisher at similar scale; we can share anonymized benchmarks and a reference contact if needed. 
07:55 Daniel: Great. Any open questions from Redwood side? 
07:58 Liam: One last technical — do you have tokenization differences or domain-specific embeddings that might affect recall? 
08:04 Priya: We do have some domain tokens (medical codes) which seem to reduce recall sometimes. We'll include sample docs. 
08:12 Samira: OK to recap next steps — Samira will send pricing and security docs, Liam will send benchmark runbook and example configs, Elysium will share sample data and query trace. We'll schedule POC kick-off week of 2027-04-11. 
08:28 Marcus: Sounds good.

Notes: There's occasional transcription noise. 'K V cache' appeared as 'K V cash' in auto transcript. References: shared files link: (redwood.com/poc/elysium-benchmark) [note: placeholder link], security pack link: (redwood.com/security/soc2)
